arxiv-2202-13901.title: Measurements of jet observables sensitive to b b -quark fragmentation in t ​ t ¯ t\bar{t} events at the LHC with the ATLAS detector
arxiv-2202-13901.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2202-13901.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by The ATLAS Collaboration. Several observables sensitive to the fragmentation of b b -quarks into b b -hadrons are measured using 36 fb -1 of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV proton–proton collision data collected with the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

arxiv-2203-05705.title: DNN Training Acceleration via Exploring GPGPU Friendly Sparsity
arxiv-2203-05705.creator: Zhuoran Song, Yihong Xu, Han Li, Naifeng Jing, Xiaoyao Liang, Li Jiang
arxiv-2203-05705.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Zhuoran Song, Yihong Xu, Han Li, Naifeng Jing, Xiaoyao Liang, Li Jiang. The training phases of Deep neural network (DNN) consumes enormous processing time and energy. Compression techniques utilizing the sparsity of DNNs can effectively accelerate the inference phase of DNNs. However, it is hardly used in the training phase because the training phase involves dense matrix-multiplication using General-Purpose Computation on Graphics Processors (GPGPU), which endorse the regular and structural data layout.

arxiv-2212-14165.title: Functional Integrative Bayesian Analysis of High-dimensional Multiplatform Genomic Data
arxiv-2212-14165.creator: Rupam Bhattacharyya, Nicholas C. Henderson, and Veerabhadran Baladandayuthapani
arxiv-2212-14165.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rupam Bhattacharyya, Nicholas C. Henderson, and Veerabhadran Baladandayuthapani. Rapid advancements in collection and dissemination of multi-platform molecular and genomics data has resulted in enormous opportunities to aggregate such data in order to understand, prevent, and treat human diseases. While significant improvements have been made in multi-omic data integration methods to discover biological markers and mechanisms underlying both prognosis and treatment, the precise cellular functions governing these complex mechanisms still need detailed and data-driven de-novo evaluations.

arxiv-2308-09747.title: Pre-equilibrium photons from the early stages of heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2308-09747.creator: Oscar Garcia-Montero, Aleksas Mazeliauskas, Philip Plaschke, Sören Schlichting
arxiv-2308-09747.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Oscar Garcia-Montero, Aleksas Mazeliauskas, Philip Plaschke, Sören Schlichting. We use QCD kinetic theory to compute photon production in the chemically equilibrating Quark-Gluon Plasma created in the early stages of high-energy heavy-ion collisions. We do a detailed comparison of pre-equilibrium photon rates to the thermal photon production.

arxiv-2311-00759.title: Logic families
arxiv-2311-00759.creator: Hajnal Andréka and Zalán Gyenis and István Németi ∗ and Ildikó Sain ∗
arxiv-2311-00759.description: Abstract A logic family is a bunch of logics that belong together in some way. First-order logic is one of the examples. Logics organized into a structure occur in abstract model theory, institution theory and in algebraic logic. Logic families play a role in adopting methods for investigating sentential logics to first-order like logics.

arxiv-2408-11806.title: Counting simplicial pairs in hypergraphs
arxiv-2408-11806.creator: Jordan Barrett, Paweł Prałat, Aaron Smith, François Théberge
arxiv-2408-11806.description: Abstract We present two ways to measure the simplicial nature of a hypergraph: the simplicial ratio and the simplicial matrix. We show that the simplicial ratio captures the frequency, as well as the rarity, of simplicial interactions in a hypergraph while the simplicial matrix provides more fine-grained details.

arxiv-2411-09816.title: Learning Fine-grained Parameter Sharing via Sparse Tensor Decomposition
arxiv-2411-09816.creator: Cem Üyük cem.ueyuek@tum.de, Mike Lasby mklasby@ucalgary.ca, Mohamed Yassin mohamed.yassin@ucalgary.ca, Utku Evci, evcu@google.com, Yani Ioannou yani.ioannou@ucalgary.ca
arxiv-2411-09816.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Cem Üyük cem.ueyuek@tum.de, Mike Lasby mklasby@ucalgary.ca, Mohamed Yassin mohamed.yassin@ucalgary.ca, Utku Evci, evcu@google.com, Yani Ioannou yani.ioannou@ucalgary.ca. Large neural networks achieve state-of-the-art performance on many tasks, yet their sheer size hinders deployment on resource-constrained devices. Among existing compression approaches, cross-layer parameter sharing remains relatively unexplored for transformer models. In this paper, we introduce Fine-grained Parameter Sharing (FiPS), a unified framework for compressing transformer Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) that combines cross-block parameter sharing, low-rank factorization, and sparsity in a single optimization.

arxiv-2502-07608.title: Time2Lang: Bridging Time-Series Foundation Models and Large Language Models for Health Sensing Beyond Prompting
arxiv-2502-07608.creator: Arvind Pillai, Dimitris Spathis, Subigya Nepal, Amanda C Collins, Daniel M Mackin, Michael V Heinz, Tess Z Griffin, Nicholas C Jacobson, Andrew Campbell
arxiv-2502-07608.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) show promise for health applications when combined with behavioral sensing data. Traditional approaches convert sensor data into text prompts, but this process is prone to errors, computationally expensive, and requires domain expertise. These challenges are particularly acute when processing extended time series data.

arxiv-2506-13775.title: On the scalar tachyons creation in noncommutative de Sitter space-time
arxiv-2506-13775.creator: Slimane Zaim
arxiv-2506-13775.description: Abstract We investigate tachyon production in noncommutative de Sitter space by solving the deformed Klein-Gordon equation. Using the Bogoliubov transformation method, we compute the number density of created scalar tachyons and demonstrate that their spectrum follows a thermal distribution. Our analysis reveals that noncommutativity reduces the effective temperature of tachyon production, analogous to its effect on ordinary particle creation.

arxiv-2511-11016.description: Abstract The interior transmission eigenvalue problem (ITP) plays a central role in inverse scattering theory and in the spectral analysis of inhomogeneous media. Despite its smooth dependence on the refractive index at the PDE level, the corresponding spectral map from material parameters to eigenpairs may exhibit non-smooth or bifurcating behavior.

pmc-12813635.creator: Yeongtaek Hwang, Paul Kim, Minji Kwon, Sung-Vin Yim, Bo-Hyung Kim, Hyunjung Lim, Icro Maremmani
pmc-12813635.description: Background/Objectives: Excessive alcohol consumption leads to hangovers, which cause discomfort and reduce work efficiency, resulting in socioeconomic losses. pmc-13165283.title: Inhibition Mechanism, Multi-Target Regulation, and Protective Effects of Camel Casein ACE-Inhibitory Peptide on HUVECs Cells
pmc-13165283.creator: Fei Zhang, Hao Miao, Chenkun Huo, Ruiqi He, Yanan Qin, Jie Yang, Zhongkai Zhao
pmc-13165283.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hypertension is a severe global public health issue. Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE)-inhibitory peptides have shown great potential as safe and effective alternatives to synthetic antihypertensive drugs. Camel milk is rich in bioactive peptides. This study aimed to screen for ACE-inhibitory peptides from hydrolyzed camel casein, explore their inhibitory mechanisms and endothelial protective effects in vitro, and reveal their potential antihypertensive pathways using network pharmacology.

pmc-13292194.creator: Evelyn Ling Lee, Eng‐Seng Chan, Lee Fong Siow, Cher Pin Song, Yee‐Ying Lee
pmc-13292194.description: Structured lipids (SLs) have attracted growing industrial interest due to their associated health benefits. Lipases, as highly selective and versatile biocatalysts, are central to the sustainable synthesis of SLs attributed to their ability to operate under mild reaction conditions. However, the limited operational stability of lipases remains a major bottleneck, directly affecting process efficiency, product yield, and economic feasibility.

pmc-13312650.title: Cardiotoxicity of monoclonal antibody-based therapies in breast cancer: a contemporary narrative review
pmc-13312650.creator: Ana Cláudia Aparecida Santos Nussbaum, Marcelo Antonini, André Mattar, Fernando Bacal, Juliana Monte Real
pmc-13312650.description: Monoclonal antibody-based therapies have substantially improved outcomes in breast cancer, particularly through HER2-directed treatment strategies, but have also introduced important cardiovascular toxicities that require careful recognition and management. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on cardiotoxicity associated with monoclonal antibody therapies used in breast cancer, with emphasis on HER2-targeted antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and selected immune checkpoint inhibitors.

pmc-13356276.title: Acute hypoxia impairs uphill running performance and alters metabolic responses in adult trained trail runners: A pilot study
pmc-13356276.creator: Diego Jaén‐Carrillo, Coralie Gobbo, Olivier Girard, Felipe García‐Pinillos
pmc-13356276.description: To investigate the effects of acute hypoxia on uphill running and physiological responses during a 12‐min uphill time trial in trained trail runners and to assess potential sex differences.
